source_name: Worldline SA Investor Relations (group results, MS segment)
why_relevant: Group results and universal registration document give Merchant Services segment economics and CEE commentary; Hungary is rarely broken out but disposals, impairments and terminal-base numbers frame the acquirer's Hungarian capacity and intent.

source_name: Nexi Group corporate site / investor relations
why_relevant: Nexi entered Hungary via Nexi Central Europe (2020) and Nexi Hungary Zrt. (registered Budapest, Alíz utca 3); group results and the history/transformation pages document the CEE build-out that determines Hungarian acquiring/issuing-processing share.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe - company data / country pages
why_relevant: The regional entity through which Nexi operates in Hungary; company-data pages give legal entity identifiers and registered details for the Hungarian arm, the anchor needed to pull local statutory accounts.

source_name: FinTechZone.hu (Hungarian fintech/payments trade press)
why_relevant: Reliably republishes and contextualises scheme/acquirer press releases aimed at Hungary (Mastercard Digital Payments Index, biometric payments launches, Worldline's stated ambition to be Hungarian banks' preferred payments partner) - often the only surviving copy when corporate PR pages rotate.

source_name: Privátbankár.hu - Mastercard tag archive
why_relevant: Tag-based longitudinal archive of Hungarian coverage of a scheme actor - a cheap way to reconstruct a timeline of Mastercard's Hungarian announcements and of critical/regulatory coverage the scheme itself would not publish.

source_name: Global Payments Inc. Investor Relations / SEC filings
why_relevant: Parent-level regulated disclosure for the acquirer that runs Erste's Hungarian POS estate; 8-K/10-K items have historically documented the CEE JV structure and stake changes that determine who books Hungarian acquiring revenue.

source_name: Finextra - payments deal newswire (CEE acquiring)
why_relevant: Independent payments newswire that mirrors and dates acquirer/JV announcements affecting Hungary (e.g. Global Payments/CaixaBank/Erste closing) - useful as a durable, searchable index when corporate press pages are reorganised.

source_name: Kosárérték.hu - Worldline company profile (retail/payments trade portal)
why_relevant: Hungarian retail-trade portal maintaining company profile pages for acquirers, aggregating their Hungarian announcements and merchant-facing claims; a useful pointer into Hungarian merchant-side coverage of the acquiring layer.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf – Banking Case Studies hub
why_relevant: Vendor-published customer case studies naming specific banks and their self-service/outsourcing decisions; CEE examples (e.g. CSOB) show the format. Each case study is itself a pointer to a bank-side source and to contract scope (fleet size, managed services).

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (Hungarian legal entity) – company registry profiles
why_relevant: Hungarian subsidiary (Vecses, reg. no. 01-09-690680, present since 2000). Filed annual accounts reveal revenue trajectory of the local ATM/banking-IT business, i.e. an indirect proxy for Hungarian bank self-service spend that no bank discloses.

source_name: Hungarian municipal 'kihelyezett ATM szolgáltatási szerződés' documents (e.g. Onga)
why_relevant: Municipalities publish the actual ATM placement/service contracts in their council agendas. A retrieved example names MBH Bank Nyrt. and lists Diebold Nixdorf Kft. as the bank's authorised ATM operating partner — a rare public document that directly links a systemic Hungarian bank to its ATM vendor.

source_name: NCR Atleos – corporate site (banking/ATM-as-a-Service, services)
why_relevant: Largest global ATM vendor/operator; its product, ATMaaS and managed-services pages plus newsroom are the entry point to customer wins and outsourcing deals. No Hungary-specific reference surfaced in search, so this is a monitoring hub rather than an evidence page.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide press releases on Hungarian bank ATM outsourcing
why_relevant: Named deal disclosure: 10-year ATM outsourcing extension with Budapest Bank covering its ~145-ATM network. Exactly the vendor-side trace of a Hungarian bank technology decision that never appears on a procurement portal.

source_name: GVH (Hungarian Competition Authority) proceedings against Euronet Banktechnikai Kft.
why_relevant: Competition-authority investigations into the ATM operator expose pricing, fee structures and market-position facts the vendor would never publish; GVH case files often quantify estate size and contractual practice.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. – Befektetői információk / Pénzügyi jelentések
why_relevant: Hungary's dominant listed IT integrator (2025 IFRS revenue HUF 744.8bn). Quarterly and annual reports plus segment commentary are the main public window on Hungarian banking-IT project pipelines, acquisitions and named financial-sector clients.

source_name: BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) issuer disclosure feed – 4iG company page / newkibdata
why_relevant: The statutory disclosure channel where 4iG (and any listed HU banking-tech issuer) files reports and extraordinary announcements before/independently of its own site; bet.hu newkibdata hosts the report PDFs directly and is the canonical, timestamped copy.

source_name: Dorsum Zrt. – blog / hírek and client references
why_relevant: Hungarian wealth/investment-software vendor whose own blog names its bank clients (OTP, MKB, CIB, Takarék, Raiffeisen, Magyar Államkincstár) and describes concrete implementation/migration projects (e.g. the Magyar Bankholding IT migration interview) — direct evidence of Hungarian bank IT programmes.

source_name: Portfolio.hu – 'dorsum' and banking-IT tag pages
why_relevant: Leading HU financial daily; its vendor tag pages aggregate long-form interviews with banking-IT suppliers that disclose client wins and system replacements not published elsewhere. Tag pages act as a snowball index per vendor.

source_name: MNB 19/2025. (VI.26.) ATM-telepítési rendelet + settlement/bank allocation lists
why_relevant: The regulation names, settlement by settlement, which bank must install an ATM (>=1000 inhabitants by 2025-12-31, >=500 by 2026-12-31), plus mandatory inter-bank delegation contracts (min. 5 years, signed by 2025-07-31) and escalating fines to HUF 150m. This creates a dated, bank-attributed ATM demand pipeline — the strongest public driver of vendor orders in HU.

source_name: HU bank-comparison/fintech media ATM trackers (Bank360, Bankmonitor, FinTechZone, Economx, Világgazdaság)
why_relevant: These outlets republish and tabulate the per-bank ATM installation lists and track completion (e.g. MBH reported completing its obligation ahead of deadline; OTP and MBH leading). They give dated, bank-level rollout progress that neither MNB nor the banks publish in tracker form.

source_name: Cash-Atm Banktechnikai Kft. – Hungarian independent ATM operator
why_relevant: Local independent ATM deployer/operator doing nationwide ATM operation and site management — a likely counterparty for banks delegating small-settlement ATM obligations. Only a social page surfaced, so a corporate site is unconfirmed.

source_name: Banktech Safe Kft. – banktech.hu (self-service kiosk / cash-handling distributor)
why_relevant: Positions itself as a leading domestic distributor of banking technology: safes, automated cash tills, kiosks, cash counting/authentication, access control. Its product and partner pages map which foreign cash-handling brands reach the HU market and through whom.

source_name: DBM Kft. – banktechnika / biztonságtechnika integrator
why_relevant: 30+ year Hungarian integrator covering banking technology and security technology for branch environments; reference/partner pages indicate which banks it equips and which OEM brands it represents.

source_name: Helyretesz – custom banking/customer-flow kiosk manufacturer
why_relevant: Designs and manufactures purpose-built devices for IT, banking and customer-service use (queue-management systems, information kiosks) — a domestic supplier layer to bank branch transformation projects.

source_name: CRITERION Zrt. – készpénzlogisztika / ATM üzemeltetés (CIT & cash processing)
why_relevant: Hungarian cash-in-transit and cash-management provider explicitly listing ATM operation, cash processing and value storage for banking and retail partners. Cash-logistics providers sit between banks and ATM vendors and their service pages reveal the operating model of the HU ATM estate.

source_name: Auriga S.p.A. – press releases & partner announcements (TRSYS channel covering Hungary)
why_relevant: Auriga's multivendor ATM software reaches Hungary through the TRSYS partnership (territory explicitly includes Hungary). Partner/channel announcements identify who can sell WWS to Hungarian banks — the route by which an ATM software change would occur.

source_name: ATM Marketplace – vendor company showcases (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Auriga)
why_relevant: Trade-press aggregator holding per-vendor showcase pages, product sheets and news; a compact index for discovering additional self-service vendors and their case studies, including ones with CEE footprints not visible on their own sites.

source_name: FeaturedCustomers – Diebold Nixdorf reference/review profile
why_relevant: Third-party aggregation of named customer references and testimonials for the vendor; useful to discover bank names that the vendor's own site does not surface, then to snowball back to the bank's own reporting.
